summary: The current English candidate preserves the complete source snapshot, objects, mathematics, historical quantities and source references. Its scientific qualifications are substantially appropriate, but the half-field premise and stored-energy derivation are not sufficiently explicit, and its equation substitutions and figure explanations still require knowledge that the specified independent reader does not have. Five actionable text findings prevent approval.

findings.title: State and explain equal opposite plate charge before assigning half the field
findings.evidence: The model fixes each plate's charge and declares a half-field contribution without ever saying that the two charges have equal amounts and opposite signs. Its opening also uses conducting, insulating and separated charge before concretely explaining them.
findings.impact: Broad plates and fixed charges alone do not establish equal field contributions. The child cannot infer the missing premise from an unexplained charge symbol, a diagram or an earlier section; unequal plate charges or an added external field would not support this half-field statement.
findings.action: In the existing English prose, explain charge as an electric property with positive and negative signs, conduction as allowing charge to move and insulation as keeping the two conductors electrically separated. Explicitly make the ideal facing plates carry equal amounts of opposite charge, with no added external field. Explain that each contributes an equally strong field in the same direction inside the gap, so either contribution is half the total. Preserve the original U+00A7 81 reference and every existing formula and source reference.
findings.acceptance: A reader can state what is equal, what has opposite signs, why the contributions add between the plates and why the half-field claim is conditional, using this lesson's words rather than assumed prior physics.

findings.title: Connect force, the complete gap displacement and the zero-energy reference
findings.evidence: After invoking formula (8-22), the text says a single relative displacement gives the entire stored energy. It does not say that the displacement is the initial gap d, explain why the force stays constant at fixed charge, or identify the zero-gap ideal limit as the zero of the stored energy. The definitions of work and multiplication decode notation but do not establish this reasoning.
findings.impact: For an arbitrary displacement the work is an energy change, not necessarily all the initial energy. Without the missing steps, a non-algebra reader cannot derive the retained expression, distinguish moving one plate from counting the interaction twice, or understand the sign of the work while attractive plates approach.
findings.action: Label this as an ideal thought experiment, not a handling instruction. Describe one plate held still while the other is slowly allowed toward it, or an equivalent single relative movement. At fixed charge, unchanged area and the maintained ideal material model, explain that the attraction is charge amount times the other plate's half-field and stays constant. Work for this constant force is force times distance; the complete distance is the initial gap d. Explain that stored field energy tends to zero with the gap in this ideal limit, so that full positive work equals the initial energy. Reversing that separation requires the same work. Keep reversible electrical charging distinct from this mechanical reverse process and retain the existing fixed-voltage supply/loss caveats. Explain the Ed-to-voltage replacement verbally without changing its formula.
findings.acceptance: The child can explain the direction of attraction, why d is the full relative distance, why the constant-force work gives initial stored energy, and why neither a second plate calculation nor all fixed-voltage supply energy may be added again. No new mathematical or physical erratum is asserted.

findings.title: Explain the capacitance relation and both substitutions instead of referring away
findings.evidence: The only local capacitance description is stored charge for a given voltage. Paragraph 23 asks the reader to use (8-36), but the charge-to-voltage relation is never stated. The next paragraph defines C, division and squares, then jumps to the three-way equality.
findings.impact: Knowing what a fraction bar means does not tell a child why voltage may be replaced by charge amount divided by capacitance, or charge amount by capacitance times voltage. The lesson therefore still depends on prior algebra and access to the earlier formula.
findings.action: Preserve (8-36), (8-42), (8-43) and all existing math tokens. In words, state that capacitance is charge amount divided by voltage size for the fixed linear capacitor; equivalently charge amount is capacitance times voltage size. Explain the first replacement as multiplying the charge amount by itself and dividing by capacitance and then by two. Explain the other replacement as capacitance times voltage size times that same voltage size, divided by two. Make clear that these are three ways to calculate the same energy, not three energies to add. If referring to the earlier notation, explain in words that its U voltage label and this lesson's V denote the same potential-difference quantity; do not silently replace either source symbol or add unregistered math tokens.
findings.acceptance: A child can follow both substitutions from locally stated meanings and say why q squared or V squared appears without being sent to an earlier equation or being required to solve an algebraic rearrangement.

findings.title: Bridge the unchanged apparatus and total-field symbols to the English explanation
findings.evidence: The bound Figure 158 spec describes inner and outer conducting coatings separated by glass, but N83 only calls it an early capacitor. The bound Figure 159 spec identifies left negative and right positive plate-charge labels and a leftward TOTAL field with a vector accent. N83 does not explain those signs, that direction or the accent, and introduces the half-field in the same passage as the unexplained picture.
findings.impact: A reader familiar only with the newly described flat plates cannot identify the jar's two conductors and insulating gap. A reader without physics/vector knowledge can confuse the field arrows with force or charge-flow arrows, or mistake the displayed E for the other plate's E/2 contribution.
findings.action: Add short prose-only explanations within N83. Identify the jar's inner and outer metal coatings as its two conducting surfaces and the glass between them as the insulator, using the existing bound apparatus inventory. For Figure 159, explain that the left and right signs identify opposite plate charges, bars give the amount, and the arrows indicate the total field direction from the positive plate toward the negative one. Explain that the accent above E indicates direction, whereas E in the calculation is the strength. Explicitly distinguish the total field shown from the other-plate contribution used in the force calculation. Do not claim the apparatus drawing shows a visible spark. Do not add labels, overlays or procedures to either figure, and do not edit Figure 158's N80 context or any shared spec.
findings.acceptance: Both figures are understandable from the N83 English words alone, without N80 or unexplained vector notation; unchanged figures and their original source/pixel bindings remain untouched.

findings.title: Do not split the leakage explanation into a semicolon fragment and lowercase continuation
findings.evidence: Paragraph 33 ends with operating conditions; and paragraph 34 starts they do not all lose it within the same short time. These are separate authoritative prose-flow paragraphs, not a soft visual line wrap.
findings.impact: The isolated lowercase continuation requires the child to carry an unfinished sentence across paragraph boundaries and obscures the relationship between varying leakage rates and the historical battery comparison.
findings.action: Keep the original objects and intended paragraph count by ending paragraph 33 as a complete sentence and beginning paragraph 34 with an explicit complete sentence about differing energy-retention times. Preserve the leakage qualification, historical battery limitation, all source quantities and the three concept boundaries. Recompute affected prose-flow anchors if any anchored paragraph changes.
findings.acceptance: Each displayed paragraph reads as a complete thought. The authoritative flow remains complete and its declared anchors exactly match the final text.

independentScienceAssessment.basis: Independent analysis of the retained source equations and ideal-model energy accounting, not adoption or replay of the historical Chinese science review.

halfOtherField.assessment: Conditionally valid for matched ideal facing plates with equal opposite charge, no added external field and the stated ideal gap material. Ignoring self-force and avoiding an extra interaction count are correct.
halfOtherField.missing: The English prose does not state the equal/opposite-charge premise or explain why the two contributions add; R1.
halfOtherField.dielectricLimit: The mechanical calculation assumes the ideal gap medium and its relevant properties are maintained while separation changes; material-mechanical effects outside that ideal model are not being approved.

reviewerOnlyDerivation: Write Q for the positive charge amount, A for the equal facing area and epsilon for the constant gap permittivity. These are reviewer-only explanatory quantities, not proposed source substitutions.
In the ideal model E=Q/(epsilon A), so fixed Q, area and permittivity make E constant during the relative motion.
The attractive-force magnitude is Q times E/2. For initial gap d reduced toward zero, its work is Q(E/2)d.
Taking the zero-gap limit as the zero of stored field energy gives the retained E_P=|q|(E/2)d. For a partial movement only the change in stored energy is obtained.
Moving one plate across the gap counts the interaction once. If both move, the distances add to the one change in gap; the same full-gap work is not counted twice.
Using the retained Ed=|V| gives E_P=|q||V|/2.
fixedChargeDisplacement.assessment: No formula correction needed. Explicit reasoning and energy-reference explanation are missing; R2.
fixedChargeDisplacement.physicalLimit: The zero-gap statement is an ideal limiting argument, not actual conductor contact through a real dielectric or a practical experiment.

chargingAndSupplyLosses.assessment: The revised source claim is correctly limited to reversible negligible-loss charging. The English text separately warns about fixed-voltage circuit dissipation and supply charge/energy exchange during plate motion.
chargingAndSupplyLosses.reviewerOnlyCheck: For a fixed linear initially uncharged capacitor, the reversible charging voltage grows from zero to its final value, giving stored work equal to one-half final charge times final voltage. Direct charging from a constant-voltage source is different energy accounting; the ordinary resistive case supplies final charge times voltage and dissipates the remaining half.
chargingAndSupplyLosses.limit: That ordinary resistive-case split is reviewer analysis, not a newly asserted universal loss fraction for all charging circuits. Retain the candidate's general loss qualification.
chargingAndSupplyLosses.finding: R2 requests clearer separation of mechanical reversal and electrical charging, not removal of the existing correct supply caveats.

generalLinearCapacitor.assessment: The retained three expressions are mutually consistent when capacitance is fixed with charging voltage and the capacitor is linear with negligible loss. They need not have parallel-plate geometry.
generalLinearCapacitor.reviewerOnlyCheck: Replacing voltage magnitude by charge amount divided by C gives q^2/(2C); replacing charge amount by C times voltage magnitude gives CV^2/2.
generalLinearCapacitor.limit: Do not generalize the half-product formula to nonlinear, hysteretic, voltage-dependent or lossy devices without appropriate energy accounting.
generalLinearCapacitor.finding: R3 concerns missing local meanings and substitutions for the child; the equations themselves are retained and correct under their qualified scope.

lightning.assessment: Acceptable as an explicitly rough cloud-ground capacitor analogy for separated charge, stored energy and discharge. The candidate already disclaims a complete account of every lightning event.
lightning.historicalPrice: The few-kopeks claim remains a quotation of the Soviet book's own-time rough valuation. No present-day tariff, currency conversion, typical modern flash energy or universal price is inferred.
lightning.historicalTime: 10^{-6} seconds is retained and decoded as a millionth of a second. Approval here is of its explicit historical-model attribution and warning against treating it as a whole-flash duration, not independent verification of a measured universal or typical local lightning time.
lightning.damage: Concentrated release in short time and small space is a useful qualitative explanation; the draft does not claim a complete model of lightning damage.

capacitorDischargeUse.assessment: Acceptable qualified descriptions of comparable spark devices, rapid release through a suitable circuit, camera-flash storage and discharge, leakage dependent on conditions, and historical battery/radio limitations.
limits: Spark appearance is not a calibrated measure of energy across arbitrary devices.
Discharge speed is not universally instantaneous; the capacitor and connected circuit matter.
The few-hundred-joules range and long-term battery comparison are not universal modern capacitor limits.
The safety wording around the Leyden jar must remain descriptive, and the moving-plate derivation should be explicitly a thought experiment.
capacitorDischargeUse.finding: R5 is a prose-flow repair, not a change to these qualified scientific claims.
